proposals.value: Le pays est envahi par les croisés.

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form Les croisés envahissent le pays. (same meaning). Grammatically well formed, but it is the trap form: the passive is far more common in English than in French, which prefers the active voice. The error is stylistic overuse, not ungrammaticality. Uncertainty moderate.

entity_key.title: Adjectives change meaning based on position

proposals.value: un homme grand (= un homme illustre)

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form un grand homme (= un homme illustre). Placing grand after the noun gives the physical meaning 'tall', so the postposed adjective cannot convey 'great/illustrious'. Confidence high.

proposals.value: Ce professeur est apprécié par ses étudiants.

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form Ce professeur est apprécié de ses étudiants. With verbs of emotion or opinion the agent takes de; par is reserved for a genuinely active agent, so par is the learner's overgeneralisation here. Uncertainty moderate.

proposals.value: sa roman (pour « son roman » quand le possesseur est une femme)

evidence.notes: Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they modify, not with the possessor, so roman (masculine) requires son even when the owner is female; sa roman is the classic learner error. Context gives the correct form son roman (his/her novel). Confidence high.

entity_key.title: Color adjectives from nouns are invariable

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form des chaussures marron. Marron comes from the noun (the chestnut) and stays invariable in the masculine singular, so the plural -s is the learner error. Confidence high.
Paired with the 719 correct form des yeux vert clair. Both elements of a compound colour adjective remain in the masculine singular, so agreeing either element is the learner error. Confidence high.

entity_key.title: Compound demonstrative pronouns may be derogatory

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form Celui-ci est mon collègue. Grammatically well formed, but it is the trap form: celui-ci/celui-là carry a condescending or derogatory nuance when used about an absent person, which the source warns against. Pragmatic/register error rather than a grammatical one. Uncertainty moderate.

Paired with the 719 correct form Il doit être malade. (probability). Falloir expresses obligation, not probability, so this is the learner's error when a probability is meant; the source states that devoir alone carries the obligation/probability ambiguity. Confidence moderate-high.

entity_key.title: Distinguishing imparfait and passé composé usage

evidence.notes: Paired with the 719 correct form Hier, j'ai mangé une pomme. A bounded event on a specific occasion requires the passé composé; the imparfait is for description, habit, or an interrupted ongoing action, so its use here is the learner error. Confidence high.

proposals.value: Il aura été distrait. (futur antérieur au lieu du futur simple pour une probabilité présente)

evidence.notes: The context gives Il sera distrait. (present probability) and Il aura encore brûlé le gigot. (past probability). The error is choosing the futur antérieur for a present-state probability, where the futur simple of être is required. Confidence moderate.
